title: The hypertension-NVU-cognition Axis: Mechanisms and interventions.
summary: Midlife hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for Alzheimer's disease, but the specific molecular pathways through which it contributes to cognitive decline-pathways that are partially independent of, and interact with, amyloid-β pathology-are not fully elucidated. The purpose of this study is to develop a seizure prediction framework that can jointly model complementary temporal and spectral EEG information and capture their interactions. title: Gestational age-associated differences in human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells: biological, paracrine, and neuroprotective properties.
summary: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (UCMSCs) have shown considerable therapeutic promise for neonatal brain injury. title: Different roles of brain uroguanylin and brown adipose tissue in males and females.
summary: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are major burdens on global health today. A novel therapeutic approach could involve increasing postprandial glucose utilization through the activation of brown adipose tissue (BAT). The aim of this study was to determine role of brain uroguanylin (UGN) in sex differences in BAT function. title: Intermittent reduced-dose methotrexate enabled continuation of induction therapy despite severe delayed methotrexate elimination in primary central nervous system lymphoma: a case report.
summary: High-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) is the backbone of induction therapy for primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) but may be limited by delayed elimination and renal toxicity. summary: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is traditionally considered a strictly hepatotropic virus, and its neuroinvasive potential remains controversial. title: Brain structural features of treatment resistant depression in a large Italian sample: A multimodal imaging study.
summary: Major depressive disorder is a common psychiatric condition characterized by persistent low mood, emotional dysregulation, and cognitive impairments affecting daily functioning. title: Clinical Characteristics of Children With Precocious Puberty at Al Ahsa: A Retrospective Study.
summary: Precocious puberty is a pediatric endocrine disorder characterized by the premature onset and progression of pubertal development. It may lead to accelerated growth, advanced bone age, early epiphyseal fusion, psychosocial concerns, and reduced adult height potential. Local data from Saudi Arabia remain limited. summary: Sleep spindles are a hallmark of healthy NREM sleep whose frequency, amplitude, density, duration and topography vary with brain maturation, age and disease. summary: Intracranial EEG provides high signal-to-noise ratio and spatial resolution for detecting epileptic activity, but patient-specific electrode placement leads to substantial variation in channel count and montage across subjects.
